protections: P1 (A, CVE-2020-15209): before a node's kernel runs, a non-optional input tensor whose buffer was never allocated or written (data.raw == nullptr with bytes > 0) must be refused rather than read. In the pinned code this does not exist anywhere: the per-node input loop in Subgraph::Invoke only handles delegate staleness (tensorflow/lite/core/subgraph.cc:1023-1033).

P2 (B, GHSA-jjr8-m8g8-p6wv): Reshape must not read a null-backed shape tensor through the 1-D int32 'shape from tensor' branch, while the legacy case (second input present but ignored because the shape comes from params) must keep working (tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:108-119, 75-80).
P3 (same CWE, same operator, outside A/B's guard): Reshape::Prepare must not dereference the shape-tensor pointer when input #1 is the optional index -1 (tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:134-135).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The report names Reshape, so a solver could patch only reshape.cc. Every other kernel that reads an unallocated input (for example the expand_dims memcpy) stays open, and so does Reshape's own data input at reshape.cc:170.
evidence: tensorflow/lite/core/subgraph.cc:1023-1033 (input loop checks only delegate/data_is_stale, no data.raw check)
tensorflow/lite/core/subgraph.cc:1043 (OpInvoke called unconditionally after the loop)
tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:170 (memcpy from input->data.raw)
tensorflow/lite/kernels/expand_dims.cc:111 (same memcpy pattern in another kernel)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Reshape's second input often goes unused (the shape falls back to params), so a solver who adds the generic check may exempt Reshape input #1 entirely to keep legacy models working. That leaves the 1-D int32 null-backed shape that GetOutputShapeFromTensor still reads. This is exactly the hole B reports in A's fix.
evidence: tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:110-111 (ShapeIsVector checks only non-null pointer, rank 1 and int32, not data.raw)
tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:80 (reads shape->data.i32[i])
tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:118 (non-vector shape tensors fall back to params; their data is never read)
tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:134-138 (non-constant shape makes the output dynamic, so the read is deferred to Eval at :154-155)
tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape_test.cc:95-104 (InvalidShape: a rank-2 shape tensor must keep working through the params fallback)
tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape_test.cc:144-165 (LegacyScalarOutput: legacy [0] params behaviour must keep working)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The report is about null data buffers and this is a null tensor pointer from an 'optional' (-1) index. An Invoke-time buffer check skips optional inputs (subgraph.cc:1025), and the crash happens in Prepare, before any such check runs.
evidence: tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:123 (accepts NumInputs == 2 without checking that input #1 is a real tensor)
tensorflow/lite/kernels/reshape.cc:135 (IsConstantTensor(GetInput(...)) with no null check)
tensorflow/lite/kernels/kernel_util.cc:78-84 (GetMutableInput returns nullptr for kTfLiteOptionalTensor)
tensorflow/lite/kernels/kernel_util.h:178-179 (IsConstantTensor dereferences tensor->allocation_type)
tensorflow/lite/core/subgraph.cc:568-571 (index validation lets -1 through as optional)
tensorflow/lite/core/subgraph.cc:1025-1026 (the Invoke input loop skips optional indices)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Loading is not where the crash shows. A tensor with buffer index 0 or an empty buffer becomes a valid-looking read-write tensor with a null buffer, and the planner allocates only graph inputs, variables and node outputs, so the loader looks innocent.
evidence: tensorflow/lite/interpreter_builder.cc:470 (buffer index 0 yields buffer_data = nullptr)
tensorflow/lite/interpreter_builder.cc:479-485 (an empty buffer also yields nullptr)
tensorflow/lite/interpreter_builder.cc:533-536 (such a tensor becomes ReadWrite)
tensorflow/lite/core/subgraph.cc:1263 (ReadWrite tensors start with buffer=nullptr and bytes=required_bytes)
tensorflow/lite/arena_planner.cc:124-140 (allocates graph inputs and variables)
tensorflow/lite/arena_planner.cc:161-169 (allocates node outputs only; a tensor that is only consumed is never allocated)

masking: Not code-level masking. Once T1 is closed by a generic Invoke check, T2 only stays open if the solver adds a Reshape input #1 exemption to keep legacy models working. So T2 shows up as a judgement inside the T1 fix, not as a separate site.
T3 is not masked by T1/T2. It fires in Prepare (reshape.cc:135), which runs from PrepareOpsAndTensors (subgraph.cc:1006, 897) before the Invoke input loop (subgraph.cc:1023).

conflicts.what: The natural strict fix for T1 (refuse every null-backed non-optional input at subgraph.cc:1023) also refuses a Reshape whose second input is null-backed but ignored (non-vector or non-int32, falling back to params at reshape.cc:118). That breaks a legacy must-keep-working case. Exempting Reshape input #1 wholesale reopens T2.

Refusing data.raw == nullptr without the bytes > 0 condition breaks zero-element tensors, which legitimately have no buffer (for example the shape {0} scalar case at reshape_test.cc:131-140 and reshape_test_common.h:109-111).

fairness_risks: A legacy Reshape with a second input that is never read (shape taken from ReshapeOptions) must keep working even when that input has no buffer (reshape.cc:118). A hidden test for this has to be stated in the report or the must-keep list, or a strict generic check will fail it unfairly.

Zero-element tensors (bytes == 0) have data.raw == nullptr legitimately (subgraph.cc:1263 with required_bytes 0). A rule of 'no null buffers' that ignores bytes refuses a shape that legitimate scalar reshapes need (reshape_test.cc:131-140).

String tensors are kTfLiteDynamic and have no buffer until they are filled (subgraph.cc:1248-1255). A generic check at Invoke must not refuse a string tensor produced earlier in the same graph. Fine if the check only fires for bytes > 0 and the tensor is reallocated before use, but unverified for every string op.

For T3, refusing NumInputs == 2 with input #1 == -1 is safe only if that is treated as 'no shape tensor' or as an error. Upstream behaviour for that shape is unverified, so a hidden test should accept either a clean error or the params fallback, not one specific outcome.

design.why: These are three independent fix sites with three different reasons to dismiss. T1 tests whether the solver lifts the fix from the named kernel into the shared Invoke layer (M3). T2 is the mimo-type coupled value: the legacy ignored-shape-input must keep working while the 1-D int32 null-backed shape is refused. That is exactly the A-to-B regression, and both over-hardening and over-exempting fail. T3 is the deepseek-type absent protection, with a strong dismissal argument (a pointer, not a buffer; optional index; Prepare, not Invoke) that a buffer-check fix does not close. T4 is left out as a separate trap because the T1 guard closes it; it only adds an alternative fix site. Weaknesses: there are only 3 groups (the floor), and T3 comes from outside A/B's advisories (same operator, same CWE).

unverified: The contents of the A fix (0b5662bc2be1) and the B fix (f8378920345f) are not in the pinned tree. Neither the Invoke null-buffer check nor any Reshape exemption exists here (no 'lacks data' or kTfLiteBuiltinReshape in core/subgraph.cc), so the pinned commit predates both fixes. My claim that A added a generic check in Subgraph::Invoke with a Reshape input-1 exemption, and that B narrowed that exemption to non-1-D shape tensors, comes from memory of upstream, not from the pinned code. history.a_fix_leaves_b_open and b_in_code_a_wrote rest on that.

That T3 (optional -1 as Reshape input #1 reaching IsConstantTensor(nullptr)) is reachable from a flatbuffer model end to end: the index validation and GetInput behaviour are verified, but the full load path through ParseNodes for Reshape was not traced.
Whether upstream ever fixed T3 separately (it would fit the 'nullptr checks when obtaining tensors' series, commits 1970c2158b1 and fff2c832628) is unverified.

Prepare-time reads in other kernels: the ones sampled (expand_dims.cc:83-87) gate data reads on IsConstantTensor, and MmapRo tensors always have a non-null buffer (interpreter_builder.cc:508, 526). An ordering (M7) trap was therefore not recorded, but not every kernel was checked.

Delegates: NNAPI requires a constant Reshape shape (nnapi_delegate.cc:1847-1851) and XNNPACK ignores input #1 (xnnpack_delegate.cc:159-163), so neither was recorded as a separate route. Other delegates (GPU, Hexagon, CoreML) were not checked.
